units.passage: At the UMKC Conservatory, we believe that performing arts students should explore and express the full depth of their humanity and creativity. units.passage: You will learn more if you develop your algorithms yourself and use a chatbot to verify them, rather than taking the shortcut of simply (for example) asking ChatGPT to generate the algorithms for you. In your career, there are guaranteed to be problems for which AI cannot propose algorithms or solutions. If you have not developed the critical thinking skills to develop solution algorithms on your own, you will be unable to deliver the value your employer expects from a practicing engineer.

units.passage: Our students’ success depends on their academic readiness and their development of core human capacities such as critical thinking, adaptability, communication, collaboration, creativity, empathy, emotional intelligence, ethical judgment, and the capacity to navigate ambiguity. AI may support this development, but it cannot substitute for it.
units.why: "AI may support this development, but it cannot substitute for it" says AI is limited because human capacities are built by the person, the skill-building rationale: P41.

units.passage: AI should augment human capability, not replace it. The value of a university education rests on the development of a person's own reasoning, judgment, and skill.
units.why: "The value of a university education rests on the development of a person's own reasoning, judgment, and skill" explains why AI should not replace thinking: P41.

units.passage: At the same time, we remain true to our foundational commitment to guiding students through their intellectual development and acquisition of personal academic skills.

units.passage: Ensure that AI does not replace the learning or skill development an assignment is intended to support.

units.passage: Learning vs. Efficiency: Faculty worried that over-reliance on AI might undermine the learning process by prioritizing fast outcomes over deeper engagement with material.
units.why: Reports faculty worry that "over-reliance on AI might undermine the learning process by prioritizing fast outcomes over deeper engagement". It is rationale that shortcuts displace deeper learning, not addressed to one party, so actor all, general, informs, P41.

units.passage: Just because AI can be used for an assignment or in a course does not mean that it should be. We have to consider whether the use of AI supports existing learning goals or merely provides an easy shortcut around the intentional difficulty we know is at the heart of learning. units.why: The Trainor quote says "Just because AI can be used for an assignment or in a course does not mean that it should be" and that AI may provide "an easy shortcut around the intentional difficulty we know is at the heart of learning". It is rationale that shortcuts bypass the practice that builds skill, so P41, general, informs.

units.passage: These considerations are essential as AI has the potential to harm the development of foundational skills and learning processes.
units.why: "AI has the potential to harm the development of foundational skills and learning processes" is rationale that AI shortcuts the practice that builds skill, so P41, general, informs.

units.passage: Like a runner training for a marathon, the point isn’t to just get from point A to point B, but to transform oneself along the way. A car might be faster, but it won’t build the muscle and endurance we seek.
units.why: The marathon analogy: 'the point isn't to just get from point A to point B, but to transform oneself'; AI shortcuts the practice that builds skill, P41.

units.passage: AI tools may curtail opportunities for students to develop and practice the kinds of thinking that undergird many learning goals.
units.why: 'AI tools may curtail opportunities for students to develop and practice' thinking; AI shortcuts skill-building practice, P41.

units.passage: Since basic writing, analytical, critical thinking skills are part of the learning outcomes of this course, use of ChatGPT (or other similar generative AI tools or software) is not allowed in this class for any part of a graded assignment, including generation of ideas, writing of text, rewriting your own work, or generating computer code.
units.why: Sample rationale: 'basic writing, analytical, critical thinking skills are part of the learning outcomes'; skill-building reason for the ban, P41.

units.why: CENG 41: 'The goal of this course is to foster your independent thinking, problem-solving skills'; reliance 'undermines these objectives'; skill-building reason, P41.

units.why: CENG 135: weekly assignments 'assess your individual understanding'; AI use 'contradicts the objectives'; skill-building reason, P41.

units.passage: On the other hand, when students employ AI as a substitute for the rigorous engagement with their coursework, it may bypass essential learning objectives and undermine the educational mission of the School.
units.why: When students use AI 'as a substitute for the rigorous engagement with their coursework, it may bypass essential learning objectives'; AI shortcuts skill-building, P41.

units.why: The text warns 'AI may threaten the process of learning, as commercial AI tools can generate content (e.g., a final paper) with little or no student engagement', a reason limiting AI; P41 fits.

units.passage: To support your development and independent demonstration of the course learning outcomes, generative AI use in this course is not permitted. Do not use generative AI tools or features to create, solve, summarize, translate, revise, or substantially transform work submitted for credit. Basic grammar, spelling, and punctuation features, approved assistive technologies, and approved disability accommodations are permitted unless they generate or substantially rewrite content or replace the skill being assessed. Ask before using an AI tool if you are unsure whether it is permitted. Use of generative AI outside these boundaries may be considered a violation of Texas Tech University’s Academic Integrity Policy.
units.why: The reason given is 'To support your development and independent demonstration of the course learning outcomes', i.e. doing the work yourself shows and builds skill; P41.

units.passage: Over-reliance on AI that may diminish critical thinking, writing fluency, skill development or loss of personal voice

units.passage: Engineering is a craft that you must develop over time by learning skills and building intuition.

units.passage: Third, the strength of AI is it saves us from having to spend time thinking about things, but sometimes that is precisely what we are supposed to be doing.

units.why: "AI should enhance your understanding rather than be used as a shortcut that could limit the learning" says AI shortcuts the practice that builds learning, P41.

units.why: The introduction says that 'Reliance on AI could weaken critical thinking and analytical skills if students and researchers use it as a shortcut rather than as a tool for deeper learning', which is the argument that shortcutting practice undermines learning (P41).
